subjective.question: What are the components of the Application Stack? Name the five layers.
subjective.answer: • Presentation Layer (User Interface) • Application Layer (Business Logic) • Business Layer (Data Processing) • Data Access Layer (Database Interaction) • Infrastructure Layer (Networking and Storage)

subjective.question: What is the difference between a Static Server and a Dynamic Server?
subjective.answer: Static Server | Dynamic Server Serves pre-built HTML files | Generates HTML content dynamically Fast and efficient | Supports server-side scripting (e.g. PHP, Python) Limited functionality | More flexible and interactive

subjective.question: Write JavaScript code to declare an array of the numbers 1 to 5.
Write a JavaScript function to calculate the sum of an array.

subjective.question: Explain the CSS Box Model with the help of a diagram.
subjective.answer: The CSS Box Model defines a structure that wraps around every HTML element. It has 4 main parts: • Content – where the text or images appear • Padding – the space between the content and the border • Border – the edge of the element, which comes after the padding • Margin – the space between the border and the other elements Diagram (from the outermost layer to the innermost): Margin → Border → Padding → Content. (In the source file this answer is written in Roman Urdu; it is given here in English.)

subjective.question: What is CSS? Write the basic syntax of a CSS rule with an example.
subjective.answer: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is the language used to style HTML documents. It controls the colours, fonts, spacing, borders and layout of web pages. A CSS rule consists of a selector and a declaration block: selector { property: value; } Example: h1 { color: blue; font-size: 24px; } Here h1 is the selector, and color and font-size are properties with their values.

subjective.question: What is the difference between margin and padding in the CSS Box Model?
subjective.answer: Padding is the space inside the element, between the content and the border. It increases the element's own size, and the element's background colour shows in the padding area. Margin is the space outside the element, between its border and the neighbouring elements. It is always transparent and does not add to the element's own size.

subjective.question: An element has width: 200px, padding: 10px and border: 5px. Calculate the total width the element occupies (excluding margin) according to the standard CSS Box Model.
subjective.answer: Total width = content width + left and right padding + left and right border = 200 + (2 × 10) + (2 × 5) = 200 + 20 + 10 = 230px

subjective.question: What is the difference between a class selector and an ID selector?
subjective.answer: A class selector (.name) can be applied to many elements on the same page, so it is used when the same style is needed for a group of elements. In HTML it is given as class="name". An ID selector (#name) is applied to only one unique element on a page. In HTML it is given as id="name".

subjective.question: Write CSS code that changes the background colour of a link when the user moves the mouse over it.
subjective.answer: a:hover { background-color: yellow; } :hover is a pseudo-class, so this style is applied only while the mouse pointer is over the link.

subjective.question: What does the universal selector (*) do? What is the effect of the rule * { margin: 0; padding: 0; }?
subjective.answer: The universal selector * selects every element on the page. The rule * { margin: 0; padding: 0; } removes the default margin and padding that browsers apply to elements, so the designer starts with clean, equal spacing on all elements.

subjective.question: What is JavaScript? Where does JavaScript code run?
subjective.answer: JavaScript is a programming language used to make web pages interactive and dynamic. It mainly runs inside the web browser (client-side), where it can respond to user actions, change the page content and perform calculations. With Node.js it can also run on the server.

subjective.question: Write a JavaScript function that finds and returns the largest number in an array.
subjective.answer: function findMax(array) { let max = array[0]; for (let i = 1; i < array.length; i++) { if (array[i] > max) { max = array[i]; } } return max; } console.log(findMax([85, 90, 78, 88, 95])); // Output: 95

subjective.question: What is the function of the Presentation Layer in the application stack?
subjective.answer: The Presentation Layer is the top layer of the application stack. It is the user interface (UI) — the part of the application that the user sees and interacts with, such as web pages, forms and buttons. It takes input from the user and displays the results returned by the lower layers.

subjective.question: Which layer of the application stack is responsible for database interaction? What does it do?
subjective.answer: The Data Access Layer is responsible for database interaction. It handles all communication between the application and the database: it reads data from the database and inserts, updates and deletes records, so the business logic does not have to deal with the database directly.

subjective.question: What is the role of the Infrastructure Layer in the application stack?
subjective.answer: The Infrastructure Layer is the bottom layer of the application stack. It provides the networking and storage resources — the servers, network connections and storage — on which the whole application runs.

subjective.question: Why are dynamic servers preferred for interactive websites such as login systems and online stores?
subjective.answer: A dynamic server generates HTML content at request time using server-side scripting (e.g. PHP, Python) and can fetch different data for every user from a database. Interactive websites need personalised, changing content — such as a user's own account page or shopping cart — which pre-built static pages cannot provide. That is why dynamic servers are preferred for such websites.

subjective.question: State two situations where a static server is a better choice than a dynamic server.
subjective.answer: • For simple websites whose content rarely changes, such as a personal portfolio or an information page — a static server is fast, efficient and cheap to host. • Where simplicity and security matter: a static server runs no server-side scripts and no database, so there is less that can fail or be attacked.
